situation: You meet someone new at a friend's party and want to start a conversation.
say: Hi. So... what do you do?
better: Hi, I'm Arjun. How do you know Meera? I know her from college.
also: Hi, I'm Arjun. Have you tried the kebabs yet? They're excellent.
weak: Hi, which company? What's your package?
Hello. Nice weather, no?
why: Start from what you share. It's easier to answer than a job interview question.

situation: Someone introduces themselves, and you forget their name a minute later.
say: Sorry, what's your good name again, please?
better: I'm sorry, I've forgotten your name already. Tell me once more?
also: Remind me of your name? I want to get it right.
weak: Hey... you! Hi! (avoids using any name all evening)
Your name was something with R, right? Rahul? Rohit?
why: Admitting it quickly is normal. Avoiding it all night is more awkward.

situation: At a wedding, you meet the bride's elderly relative you don't know.
say: Hello uncle, myself Priya, I am the bride's friend only.
better: Namaste, uncle. I'm Priya, Sana's friend from college. Are you from her mother's side?
also: Namaste! I'm Priya. Sana talks about her family a lot.
weak: Hi uncle. (and walks away)
Uncle, who are you exactly?
why: 'Myself Priya' is a common slip. 'I'm Priya' plus one detail is warm and clear.

situation: At a networking event, you want to ask a senior professional for advice.
say: Sir, please give me your number, I will call you for guidance.
better: I really liked your talk on supply chains. Could I email you one question about moving into that field?
also: Would you be open to a fifteen-minute call sometime next month?
weak: Sir, can you get me a job in your company?
Sir, please do the needful and guide me.
why: A small, specific request is easy to say yes to. 'Guidance' is too vague.

situation: A stranger at a party asks, "So, what's your caste?"
say: Umm... actually... we are, means, from UP side...
better: I don't really see why that matters. Tell me, how do you know the hosts?
also: I'd rather not get into that. What do you do in Hyderabad?
weak: What a backward question, are you from the stone age?
Why, what's yours first?
why: You can decline an intrusive question calmly and move the conversation on.

situation: You want to leave a conversation at a party that has gone on too long.
say: Okay, I'll just come. (and never comes back)
better: It was great talking to you. I'm going to say hi to my cousin before she leaves.
also: I'll let you get back to the party. Lovely meeting you!
weak: This is boring, I'm going.
Excuse me, I need to take an urgent call. (no call)
why: End warmly with a real reason. 'I'll just come' is a promise you won't keep.

situation: Someone at a wedding compliments your outfit.
say: Arre, no no, it's very old, just got it from Sarojini.
better: Thank you! I love the colour of your saree too.
also: Thanks so much, that's kind of you.
weak: Yes, I know, it's designer, cost me twenty thousand.
No, I look fat in this.
why: Accept a compliment with a thank you. Brushing it off makes the other person awkward.

situation: You attend a funeral and meet the grieving family.
say: Everything happens for a reason, he is in a better place now.
better: I'm so sorry. He was always kind to me. Please tell me if I can help with anything.
also: I'm so sorry for your loss. I'm thinking of you all.
weak: How did he die? Was it sudden?
At least he lived a long life, no?
why: Keep it short and sincere. Don't explain away someone's grief.

situation: A neighbour you barely know says hello in the lift.
say: Hmm. (nods and looks at phone)
better: Good morning! I'm Divya from the fourth floor. I don't think we've met properly.
also: Hi! Did the water supply come back on your floor too?
weak: Hi, which flat? Owner or tenant?
Hello. (silence for eight floors)
why: A name and one easy line turns a stranger into a neighbour.

situation: At a networking event, someone asks, "So, tell me about yourself."
say: I am basically from Patna, did my schooling there, then B.Tech, then...
better: I'm a data analyst at a health startup in Pune. Right now I'm working on predicting hospital bed demand.
also: I help small shops sell online. Lately I'm interested in rural payments.
weak: Nothing much, I'm just a normal employee.
I'm a visionary disruptor passionate about synergy.
why: Lead with what you do now and one interesting detail, not your whole history.

situation: You meet an old classmate who has become very successful.
say: Arre, big shot now! You won't remember small people like us.
better: So good to see you! I read about your company in the paper. How does it feel?
also: Congratulations on everything. Tell me, how did it all start?
weak: You were so average in school, how did you manage?
Can you give me some contacts, bro?
why: Plain warmth beats a taunt dressed up as a joke.

situation: Someone at a gathering starts a heated political argument with you.
say: You people are all brainwashed by WhatsApp university.
better: I see it differently, but I don't think we'll settle it over samosas. Let's talk cricket instead?
also: That's an interesting view. I'd rather keep tonight light, though.
weak: You're completely wrong and frankly stupid.
Ya, ya, you're right. (doesn't agree)
why: You can disagree without a fight, and choose not to debate at a party.

situation: You want to follow up with someone you met at a conference.
say: Hi, we met at that event. Please connect.
better: Hi Ritu, we spoke after your panel at the Bengaluru fintech summit. I'd love to stay in touch and hear about your project.
also: Great meeting you yesterday. Here's the article on UPI I mentioned.
weak: Hi, I'm looking for job, please refer.
Hi. 👋
why: Remind them where you met and give a reason to reply.

situation: At a wedding, you're asked to say a few words for the couple on stage.
say: I'm not a good speaker, but... umm... best wishes for the happy married life.
better: I've known Imran since we were eight. Zoya, he's loyal, funny and terrible at cooking. Look after each other. Cheers!
also: To two people who make each other better. Congratulations!
weak: I don't want to speak, someone else please.
Imran's ex would be shocked to see this day! 😂
why: Short, warm and specific beats a nervous apology. Skip embarrassing stories.

situation: Someone you just met asks how much your flat cost.
say: Uh, around... it was some 80-90 lakh, with loan and all.
better: We got a decent deal, I think! Are you looking to buy in this area?
also: Prices have gone crazy, haven't they? We're just happy to have a place.
weak: None of your business.
Why, are you from the income tax department?
why: You can skip the number and turn the question back to them kindly.

situation: At a party, you meet someone whose job you don't understand.
say: Oh, nice, nice. (nods, no idea what it is)
better: I've never heard of that. What does a normal day look like for you?
also: That sounds interesting. Explain it to me like I'm in Class 8?
weak: Is that even a real job?
Oh, so how much does it pay?
why: Curiosity is a gift. Asking makes people feel interesting.

situation: You're running late to a friend's housewarming party.
say: On the way, five minutes! (still at home)
better: Running about forty minutes late, sorry! Start without me, I'll bring dessert.
also: Leaving now, I'll be there by eight thirty.
weak: Traffic is very bad, I'm stuck. (just leaving)
(no message, arrives an hour late)
why: An honest time lets people plan. 'Five minutes' fools no one.

situation: A guest at a wedding asks why you're not married yet.
say: Haha, no one wants me, aunty, what to do.
better: It'll happen when it happens, aunty. Today I'm just enjoying the food and dancing!
also: I'm in no hurry. Isn't the decor lovely?
weak: Marriage is a scam, aunty.
Why are you asking, do you have someone for me?
why: Light and confident. No self-mocking and no lecture needed.

situation: Someone at a gathering keeps interrupting you while you speak.
say: Haan, haan, you say, you say. (gives up)
better: Let me just finish this point, then I really want to hear yours.
also: One second, I'm almost done.
weak: Can you shut up for one minute?
(stops talking for the rest of the evening)
why: Hold your turn politely. You don't need to be loud to be heard.

situation: You meet a friend's spouse for the first time.
say: Oh, so you're the famous wife! He never stops complaining about you. 😄
better: So lovely to finally meet you, Ananya! Karthik talks about you all the time.
also: I've heard so much about you, all good, I promise.
weak: Hi. So, arranged or love?
You're much prettier than he said.
why: A warm first line sets the tone. Jokes about their marriage can land badly.

situation: You're at a party where you know only the host, and feel awkward.
say: (stands near the snacks scrolling Instagram all night)
better: Hi, I only know Rhea here. Mind if I join you? I'm Kabir.
also: Hi, I'm Kabir. Is this your first time at one of Rhea's parties too?
weak: (asks the host to introduce you to everyone, one by one)
I don't know anyone, this is so boring.
why: Saying you know no one is honest and gives people an easy way in.

situation: At a networking event, someone gives you their card and asks for yours.
say: Sorry, I don't have card, I'm just a fresher, nothing special.
better: I don't have cards on me. Can I add you on LinkedIn? I'm Shreya, I've just started as a UX designer.
also: Let me scan your QR and send you a message right now.
weak: Cards are outdated, no one uses them.
Nothing special about me, sorry.
why: Never shrink yourself. Offer a simple way to connect.

situation: Someone you met makes a comment about your region's food or language.
say: Haha ya, we South Indians only eat idli-dosa. (forced laugh)
better: Ha, there's a lot more than idli! You should try Chettinad food sometime, I'll take you.
also: That's a common idea. Kerala and Tamil Nadu food are very different, actually.
weak: You North Indians only know butter chicken.
That's such a racist thing to say.
why: Correct the stereotype with warmth and an invitation, not a counter-stereotype.

situation: An acquaintance asks you to buy a product from their new MLM business.
say: Ya, sure, I'll see, send me details. (never will)
better: Thanks for thinking of me, but I won't be buying. Good luck with it, though.
also: It's not for me, but I'm happy to catch up over coffee.
weak: MLM is a scam, you'll lose money.
Maybe next month, after my salary. (every month)
why: A kind, clear no saves both of you endless follow-ups.

situation: You want to invite a new colleague to a weekend outing with your friends.
say: If you are free, then only come, no compulsion.
better: A few of us are going to Nandi Hills on Saturday morning. Would love it if you joined!
also: We're doing a dosa breakfast on Sunday. Want to come along?
weak: You can come if you want, I don't know if others will like it.
You probably won't come, but still asking.
why: A warm, specific invite makes people feel wanted, not tolerated.
